1yy5l3x: The Buddha taught: "Like an iron smelter filtering out the remaining residue of refined iron and crafting exquisite utensils. People who study the Dharma must remove their polluted minds and their deeds will become pure." Sutra forty-two chapters

995e74: There was a monk who recited the Amitabha Buddha Sutra at night, his voice sad, as if regretfully retreating. The Buddha asked: "In the past, what did you usually do when you were at home?". He replied: "I like to play the harp." Buddha asked: "What happens when the strings of the guitar are loose?". The response was: "I can't call." Question: "What if the strings are too tight?". The response was: "The voice is lost." Ask: "What if it's not tight or loose?". Answer: "The sounds are complete." The Buddha taught: "The same is true for monks who study the Dharma. If their psychology is balanced, then they can attain the Dharma. Too much stress in cultivating the Dharma makes the body tired. When the body is tired, the mind will give rise to afflictions. If the mind gives rise to afflictions, the virtue will retreat. When the virtue has retreated, the sins will increase. Only with purity and peace can the Dharma not be lost." Sutra forty-two chapters
180ceau: The Buddha asked a monk: "How long does a human life last?". The answer was: "Within a few days." Buddha said: "You do not understand the way." 10f7vh0: The Buddha taught: "Monks who practice the Dharma should not be like an ox working hard; although the body is practiced, the mind is not practiced. If the mind is practiced, there is no need for the body to practice (according to the external form)." Sutra forty-two chapters

1feroxy: There are families, monks, in which children pay homage to their parents at home, but that family is accepted as equal to Brahma. irdsrd: "Once, the Buddha was in Anathapindika garden, Jeta forest, Savatthi country. wpcik1: The Buddha gently taught: - Good men and women of faith, it is inevitable and reasonable for you to be confused and doubtful. In such a case, you should not rush to believe or reject the views of any religion, when you have not thoroughly understood that religion. Dear good men and women of Kalama, on this occasion the Tathagata will explain the ten foundations of true faith. Firstly, don't rush to believe anything just because it's a legend. Second, don't rush to believe something just because it belongs to tradition. Third, don't rush to believe something just because it is mentioned or propagated by many people. Fourth, don't rush to believe something just because it's recorded in scriptures or books. Fifth, don't rush to believe something just because it belongs to metaphysical theory. Sixth, don't rush to believe something just because it fits your stance. Seventh, do not rush to believe anything, when it is based on superficial data. Eighth, don't rush to believe something just because it fits your prejudices. Ninth, do not rush to believe something just because it is supported by strength and authority. Tenth, don't rush to believe anything just because it is preached by missionaries or teachers.
1kh2moj: At one time, the World-Honored One lived among the Vajji people, in the village of Bhanda. There, the World-Honored One called the Bhikkhus: There are four types of people, monks, existing in the world. What is four? There are people who go with the flow, there are people who go against the stream, there are people who stop themselves and there are people who have crossed over to the other shore, standing on land. Monks, what is the class of people who go with the flow? The type of person who enjoys sensual pleasures and commits evil karma is called going with the flow. What is the type of person who goes against the flow? Monks, there are people who do not enjoy sensual pleasures, do not do evil karma, and live a perfect and pure Pham Hanh life called going against the current. Monks, what is a person who stops by himself? People who, by destroying the five fetters, are reborn and will no longer return to this life are called self-restraints. What is the type of person who has crossed over to the other shore, standing on land? Monks, there is a class of people who, by destroying all the defilements, realize and dwell in the freed mind of the asrava, the liberated wisdom is said to have crossed over to the other shore, standing on land. Monks, there are four such classes of people present in the world. (DTKVN, Sangha Bodhisattva I, chapter 4, chapter Bhandagàma, section On the flow, published by VNCPHVN, 1996, p.557)
pxrj1y: How good, monks! We also did not see or hear the butcher, after killing the goats, pigs, cows... enjoying and living among great properties. Why? 10rhtva: At one time, the World-Honored One residing at Baranàsi, in the Deer Park, called out to the Bhikkhus: Accomplished with the three branches, Bhikkhus, it is not long before a trader achieves great and vast wealth. What is three? Here, monks, the trader has eyes, skillfully strives and builds the foundation. What is a trader with eyes? Here, monks, the merchant knows the commercial products. This thing is bought like that, sold like that, and the profit will be like that. What does a good trader strive for? Here, monks, the merchant skillfully buys and sells commercial products. And how does a businessman build the basics? Here, monks, the trader is known to the homeowners or the children of the homeowners, is known to the rich, has a lot of money, and has great assets as follows: This trader is a person with eyes, skillful in striving, has enough strength to support his wife and children, and often pays us profits. We give goods to this person: Hey merchant, take this money, build assets to support your wife and children, and often pay us interest. Thus, monks, a trader can build the basics. Accomplished with these three branches, monks, the trader will soon reach great and vast assets. (ĐTKVN, Sangha Branch I, chapter 3, chapter The wheelwright, section The trader [excerpt], published by VNCPHVN, 1996, p.207)
1knm3x5: "Once the Buddha was in the country of Xa-veti, Jeta forest, Anathapindika garden. At that time, the World-Honored One told the Bhikkhus: Giving alms at the right time has five things: Giving alms to people from afar; giving alms to those who are far away; giving alms to the sick; giving alms when in need; if you get a new fruit tree or new grain, first give it to someone who diligently observes the precepts, then eat it. That is, Bhikkhu! Correct alms-giving. At that time, there were these five things.
mjamna: Monks, there are three types of men who appear and are present in this world. What is three? Prosperous birth, dependent birth and paralyzed birth. Monks, what is a son of good birth? Here, the child's parents do not take refuge in the Buddha, do not take refuge in the Dharma, do not take refuge in the Sangha, do not give up killing, do not give up taking what is not given, do not give up evil conduct in sensual pleasures, do not give up lying, do not give up indulging in alcohol and cooking wine, and following evil precepts. As for their son, he took refuge in the Buddha, took refuge in the Dharma, took refuge in the Sangha, renounced killing, renounced taking what is not given, renounced evil conduct in sensual pleasures, renounced lying, renounced indulging in alcohol, kept the precepts according to good dharma. Monks, what is a naturally born son? Here, the child's parents take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha, abstain from killing, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from evil conduct in sensual pleasures, abstain from lying, abstain from indulging in alcohol, keep the precepts according to good dharma. Their son also took refuge in the Buddha, took refuge in the Dharma, took refuge in the Sangha, renounced killing, renounced taking what is not given, renounced evil conduct in sensual pleasures, renounced lying, renounced indulging in alcohol, and kept the precepts according to good dharma. Monks, what is a son who is born paralyzed? Here, the child's parents take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, take refuge in the Sangha, abstain from killing, abstain from taking what is not given, abstain from evil conduct in sensual pleasures, abstain from lying, abstain from indulging in alcohol, keep the precepts according to good dharma. And their son does not take refuge in the Buddha, does not take refuge in the Dharma, does not take refuge in the Sangha, does not give up killing, does not give up taking what is not given, does not give up evil deeds in sensual pleasures, does not give up lying, does not give up indulging in alcohol, the evil precepts following evil dharma.
6qdkr2: At one time, the World-Honored One was staying at Sàvatthi, at Migàrà's castle. Then Visàkhà, Migàrà's mother, came. After bowing and sitting down to one side, the World-Honored One said to Visàkhà: Visàkhà, complete with four dharmas, a woman achieves victory in this life. This life falls within her reach. What is four? Here, Visàkhà, a woman has the ability to skillfully do work, know how to hire servants, act to please her husband, and know how to preserve property. Achieving these four dharmas, Visàkhà, a woman achieves victory in this life. This life falls within her reach. Visàkhà, complete with four dharmas, a woman achieves victory in the next life. The next life falls into her hands. What is four? Here, Visàkhà, a woman is full of faith, full of virtue, full of almsgiving, full of wisdom. Achieving these four dharmas, Visàkhà, a woman will achieve victory in the next life. The next life falls within her reach. (DTKVN, Sangha Bodhisattva III, chapter 8, chapter On Men's Precepts, part In this life [summary], published by VNCPHVN, 1996, p.644)
6vqhx9: "At one time, the Buddha was in the Bamboo Garden, Calanda area, Rajagaha. At that time, after midnight, the World-Honored One heard a wild fox cry. The next morning, the World-Honored One spread out a seat, sat in front of the assembly, and asked the Bhikkhus: - At the end of the night, did you hear the wild fox cry? The Bhikkhu told the Buddha: - World-Honored One, you heard it. The Buddha told the Bhikkhu: - That wild fox was miserable because of scabies, so it had to cry. If someone treats its scabies for that wild fox, the wild fox will be grateful and repay it. Now there is a foolish person who does not know how to remember gratitude and repay gratitude. Therefore, the Bhikkhus need to learn like this: Be grateful and repay gratitude. If there is a small favor, you will not forget it, let alone a great favor. After the Buddha spoke this sutra, the Bhikkhus heard what the Buddha taught and happily followed it.

1rvp67c: There were Brahmins who came to ask the Buddha: – Venerable Gautama! After your disciples die, can you pray for them to be reborn in a good land? The Buddha did not answer but asked again: - Your disciples die, can you pray for them to be reborn in a good land? They replied: - Yes. The Buddha immediately used an example: like there is a deep well, a person rolls a large stone over the mouth of the well, then invites a few dozen Brahmin monks to come and ask: I push this stone into the well, please pray for it not to sink. The Brahmin monks replied: - No. The Buddha asked: - Why? The monks replied: - Because the heavy stone must sink to the bottom of the well, even if thousands of people pray, it will not work. The Buddha again used an example: - If someone poured oil into the well, then asked the monks to come and pray for the oil to sink to the bottom of the well, can you do it? The Brahmin monks replied: - No. Buddha asked: - Why? The monks replied: - Because the oil is light, so it must be done? floating, no matter how many people pray for it to sink, it will not sink. Buddha said: - In the same way, if people do good, do good things, even if you try to pray for them to fall into hell, they will not fall. As for people who do evil and commit too many crimes, no matter how much they pray, they cannot be born in a good world.
fqp9mk: At one time, the World-Honored One, residing in Sàvatthi, at Jetavana, called out to the Bhikkhus: Bhikkhus, there are these four fears. What is four? Fear of blaming oneself, fear of others blaming, fear of punishment, fear of evil beasts. What is fear and self-blame? Here, monks, there are people who consider: "If my body does evil, my words are evil, my mind thinks evil, then I myself can blame myself: Why did I do that karma?". Out of fear, that person blames himself, abandons evil and does good, and lives a pure life. Monks, this is called fear of self-blame. What is fear of others' blame? Here, monks, there are people who consider: "If my body does evil, my words are evil, my thoughts are evil, then others can blame me: Why do I do that karma?". That person is afraid of being blamed by others, abandons evil and does good, and lives a pure life. Monks, this is called fear of others' blame. What is fear of punishment? Here, monks, someone sees kings, when they catch thieves and robbers, and use many different punishments. They beat them with whips, sticks, and even beheaded them with swords. Because he is afraid of punishment, he does not steal other people's property. Monks, this is called fear of punishment. What is fear of evil beasts? Here, monks, someone thinks like this: "Those who do evil, speak evil words, or think evil will have evil retribution in the future." That person, because of fear of evil beasts and hell, should completely cut off his body from doing evil, speaking evil words and thinking evil thoughts. Monks, this is called fear of evil beasts. Monks, there are four types of this fear. (DTKVN, Sangha Branch II, chapter 4, chapter Fear, section Self-blame [outline], published by VNCPHVN, 1996, p.46)

1k3uuq5: "Once, the Buddha was in the country of Xa-veti, Jeta forest, Anathapindika garden. At that time, the World-Honored One told the Bhikkhus: - There are six powers in the world. 1jykd56: At one time the World-Honored One was staying at Rajagaha, at Veluvana. gom7mk: At one time, the World-Honored One resided in Vesali, at Mahavana, and taught the Bhikkhus: Accomplishing the five factors, Bhikkhus, the words are good teachings, not evil teachings, do not make mistakes and are not criticized by wise people. jetliv: "Once the Buddha came to Ba-ki-sau, in Ngac forest Bo mountain, Deer Park. At that time, the Venerable Xa-le Tu said to the monks: - Venerable monks, there are four types of people in the world. What are the four? Or there is a type of person who truly has no impurity inside but does not know, does not know that there is truly no impurity inside. Or there is a type of person who is truly impure inside and knows that there is truly no impurity inside. - Venerable Friends, if a person truly has impurity inside but does not know, does not know that there is defilement inside, then among humans, this person is the lowest person. If a person truly has impurity inside but knows that there is defilement inside, he knows that there is defilement inside If there really is impurity inside, then among humans, this person is the highest. If there is a person who truly has no impurity inside but does not know and does not know that there is really no impurity inside, then among humans, this person is the lowest person. If there is a person who truly has no impurity inside and knows and knows that there is really no impurity inside, then among humans, this person is the most superior. [excerpt])
mgwixj: "Once the Buddha was in the country of Sāvatthi, Jeta forest, Anathapindika garden. At that time, the World-Honored One told the Bhikkhus: - A person in an evil group will know by five things. Having seen five things, he knows that this person is in an evil group. What are the five? Worthy of laughing but not laughing, worthy of joy but not rejoicing, worthy of generating loving-kindness but not generating loving-kindness, doing evil but not ashamed, hearing good words without paying attention. You should know that this person is of an evil group. If there is one, you should know that this person is in an evil group. Living beings in the evil group should know by using the five things. - People in the right group will know by the five things. Having seen the five things, you will know that this person is in the right group. What is worthy of laughter, then be happy, worthy of joy, then be compassionate, worthy of shame, then be ashamed. You should know that this person is in the right group, residing in the right group. Thus, Bhikkhus, you should learn this A-ham, volume II, chapter Ta Tu, published by VNCPHVN, 1998, p.357)
11cttba: "Often happily cultivating wisdom but not cultivating almsgiving, in the next life you will be intelligent but poor without wealth; only happily cultivating almsgiving but not cultivating wisdom, in the next life you will be rich but know nothing; Almsgiving and wisdom are both cultivated, in the next life you will be rich but have wisdom. Neither almsgiving nor wisdom will be cultivated, many lifetimes will be foolish and poor." Sutra on Distinguishing Karma
78s3fl: At one time the World-Honored One was staying among the people of Sumbha, in the town of Sedaka. There, the World-Honored One taught the Bhikkhus: - Bhikkhus, suppose there was a large crowd gathered to look at a beauty queen dancing and singing with all her charm. Then a person came, wanting to live and not wanting to die. They said to him: "Hey man, look here. This is a bowl full of oil. Take that bowl full of oil and go around the large crowd and the beauty queen. A person holding a sword raised high will follow behind you. Wherever you spill a little oil, that's where your head will fall." - Monks, what do you think, that person may not pay attention? When you reach the bowl of oil, do you let your mind wander outward? - No, World-Honored One. - I say this example, monks, to clearly state the meaning of mindfulness of the body. Therefore, you need to study as follows: "We will practice mindfulness of the body, make it full, make it continue to dwell peacefully..." (ĐTKVN, Samyutta Ministry V, chapter 3, chapter Nàlanda, section Nationality, Religious Publishing House, 2002, p. 266).
ddtba6: Buddha taught: Eating too much, gaining weight, shortening life span: At one time, the World-Honored One lived in Savatthi. At that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala often ate sumptuous meals. Then, after eating, King Pasenadi, full and satisfied, went to pay homage to the World-Honored One and sat down to one side. After the World-Honored One knew that King Pasenadi had finished eating, was full, and satisfied, he immediately spoke the verse: People are often mindful. When they eat, they know what is right. In moderation, feeling strong. Old age is slow, longevity is long. At that time, King Pasenadi immediately called the young Brahmin Sudassana standing behind him: Hey friend, memorize the verse. from the World-Honored One, and while preparing food for me, read that verse, I will give you one hundred gold coins every day. Young man Sudassana obeyed the king, learned the verse by heart and every time he served food to the king he often recited this verse. Then King Pasenadi gradually limited his eating and drinking until he only ate one nālika at most. After a while, the king's body became healthy, he massaged his limbs and said the following words of inspiration: Oh, the World-Honored One truly thought of my benefit, both in the present and the future! (ĐTKVN, Tuong Ung Volume I, chapter 3, chapter 2, Great Food section, VNCPHVN publication, 1993, p.186)
1mdvxfi: The Buddha taught: "A person who gives alms, when he becomes a god or a human, surpasses a person who does not give alms in five aspects, which are longevity, beauty, peace, name, and monks" (chapter V, chapter Sumana); and "There are people who give alms with a mind without expectation, alms with an unattached mind, alms without the thought "I will enjoy this in the next life", only alms with the thought "it is good to give". He gives alms to adorn his mind. Because of such almsgiving, after the body breaks up after death, he is born and resides with the Devas in the Brahma world. When his karma is ended, his divine power, fame and authority are ended, he becomes a Non-returner, not returning to the state of non-returner. this state" (chapter VII, chapter on Altar). Sutra of Sangha branch.
100tqmb: The Buddha taught: "Monks, there are these seven assets. What are the seven? Faith, precepts, mental talent, precious wealth, literary talent, giving, wisdom. Monks, these are the seven assets. Here, the Holy disciple has faith and trust in the Tathagata's enlightenment: "This is the World-Honored One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, Complete in Wisdom and Conduct, Good Tathagata, Understanding the World, The Supreme Being, the Ruler of the Man, the Teacher of Gods and Men, the World-Honored Buddha." This is called wealth. What is the precept of wealth? Here, the Holy Disciple abstains from killing, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from evil conduct in sensual pleasures, abstains from lying, abstains from double-tongued speech, abstains from evil speech, abstains from idle talk, abstains from indulging in alcohol and boiled wine. This is called precepts. What is lascivious wealth? Here, the Holy Disciple is ashamed and embarrassed towards The body does evil, the mouth speaks evil, the thoughts are evil, the shame of having accomplished evil, unwholesome dharmas. This is called greedy wealth. What is wealth? Here, the Holy disciple has fear, fear of the body doing evil, the mouth speaks evil, thoughts of fear because of accomplishing evil, unwholesome dharmas. This is called wealth. What is wealth? Here, the Holy disciple hears a lot, preserves what he has heard, stores up what he has heard, those dharmas, at first. good, middle-class, good-natured, full of meaning, promoting a completely pure life of Pham Hanh; he has heard a lot of these dharmas, has kept them, memorized them, recited them many times, attentively observed them, and accomplished them skillfully through right understanding. This is called talent. What is almsgiving? Here, the Holy disciple with a mind that abandons the defilements of greed, lives at home and is equanimous, with open hands, likes to let go, is ready to be asked, likes to share. alms. This is called giving wealth. What is wisdom wealth? Here, the Holy disciple has wisdom, has wisdom about birth and death, and achieves the Holy Body (determination) leading to the true cessation of suffering. This is called wisdom wealth. (Sangha Nikaya Sutra, chapter seven dharma, chapter 1 - wealth chapter).
q81pp4: The Buddha taught: "There are five benefits of almsgiving: being liked and admired by many people; being close to gods and true beings; good rumors are spread; there is no deviation from the homeowner's dharma; when the body breaks up and dies, one is born in a good realm, the heavenly world." Sutra of Sangha Branch II
1ukv48x: Buddha taught that there are three types of giving: giving of material things, giving of Dharma, and giving of fearlessness. Giving alms of wealth is to eliminate greed. Giving the Dharma is to eliminate ignorance. Giving without fear is to destroy anger. Everything comes from the four minds of immeasurable love, compassion, joy, and equanimity. Compassionate mind to save sentient beings. Be happy and let go to liberate yourself. So giving alms is truly a superior practice. Among these three types of alms, the Buddha emphasized Dharma giving - Dharma giving - as in the Dhammapada, Buddha taught: "Dharma giving surpasses all giving".
